display.title: The Caliph's Secretary, Part 1
display.summary_short: Sold as a slave in Baghdad, young Dina becomes secretary to the Caliph while her father, disguised as a beggar, plans her escape. This part ends as the Jewish leaders await trial.
display.summary_long: Chacham Nissim, leader of the Jews of Alexandria, and his daughter Dina are captured by pirates and brought to the slave market of Baghdad in the days of the Caliph al-Mamun. The Jews of nearby Samarra, led by the Rav, Mar Yaakov, and the court doctor Hakim Isaac, cannot pay the slave trader's huge price, and before dawn the powerful courtier Al-Kisai carries Dina away. Her father escapes by leaping into the river and hides in Mar Yaakov's house. Dina, thirteen and motherless, is cared for by Al-Kisai's kind wife, who tells her to hide that she is Jewish. Her wisdom and handwriting make her Al-Kisai's 'little secretary' and then the Caliph's. Disguised as a beggar at the palace gate, her father finds her, and she sends him her mother's kerchief as a sign. When Al-Kisai wins a decree expelling the Jews, Dina hopes to help like Esther. Then a daring rescue plan is betrayed, the Jewish leaders are thrown into chains, and the Jews everywhere fast and daven as the day of the trial arrives.
display.lesson: Hashem guides every step with hashgachah pratis; a Jewish child keeps her Yiddishkeit even in a palace far from home.

advisories.note: Jewish captives are sold as slaves and a thirteen-year-old girl is torn from her father; she is treated kindly.
A courtier wins a decree expelling all Jews; the community leaders are chained and imprisoned.
A fight on the slave ship; the father leaps into the river to escape.
Dina's mother and the courtier's only daughter have passed away (mentioned).
Ends with the Jewish leaders in prison awaiting trial.

characters: Mar Yaakov, the Rav of Samarra
